answer: A marketplace can require every agent to escrow a scarce token before bidding, then slash part of that bond when a randomly audited task is proven fraudulent. Creating a hundred identities does not create more bonded capital: it divides the attacker’s stake, limits each account’s influence, and puts funds at risk for every bid. The attacker pays an opportunity cost even when honest, while repeated fraud can spiral into losses; reputation earned through verified work, not a nectar-like burst of new accounts, carries forward over a longer horizon.
